question: When powerful AI becomes much cheaper, who gains the most, and who might be left behind?
reflection: Cheaper intelligence can open doors for small teams and poorer regions, if we also invest in the skills to use it well.

sources.subject: Claude Opus 5.5 cuts costs, boosts coding
Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5: 40% cheaper, 30% faster output

one_line: Anthropic and OpenAI cut the price of top-tier models on the same day, while local resistance to data centres grows in the US.

top_stories.title: Two leading labs cut model prices together
top_stories.what: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, which it says costs about 40% less on typical work, and OpenAI released cheaper GPT-6 Sol and Luna models at half the earlier API prices.
top_stories.why: Lower prices make large text analysis projects, such as coding thousands of survey answers, affordable for small research teams.

top_stories.title: Local opposition stalls US data centres
top_stories.what: A tracking group reports that local opposition has blocked or delayed 45 US data-centre projects worth about $68 billion, over power, water and land.
top_stories.why: Community acceptance is becoming a real constraint on AI infrastructure, and it can be studied and planned for.

top_stories.title: Microsoft takes down an AI-run fraud service
top_stories.what: Microsoft says it disrupted a criminal service that used AI to read stolen inboxes, pick impersonation targets and plan payment fraud across thousands of organisations.
top_stories.why: AI is making email fraud more targeted, so staff training on trust cues and verification needs updating.

saudi_lens.text: The US backlash shows that data-centre plans need community buy-in on water and power; Saudi projects can plan early engagement and clear local benefits to avoid similar friction.

idea.title: Data-centre community acceptance study
idea.pitch: Map what nearby residents worry about and value when a large data centre is planned, and test which local benefits build trust.
idea.first_step: Collect public reasons given for blocked projects and group them into a short list of concerns.

idea_kids.title: Spot the trick email game
idea_kids.pitch: A card game where children compare pairs of messages and find the clues that show which one is a trick asking for secrets.
idea_kids.first_step: Write ten message pairs in Arabic and English with one clear warning sign in each fake.

concepts.summary: Top labs cut prices sharply for models near the frontier.
Local groups block or delay data centres over power, water and land.
Criminals use AI to scale fraud, and companies use legal and technical action to stop them.
